chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Abu Sa'id al-Qammāt, from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: If a man intends to perform Hajj but is unable to do so, and he goes to the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and performs the 'Arafah standing (at his grave), that will suffice for him in place of Hajj.

key_terms.عَرَفَ: To stand at 'Arafah (a pillar of Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the grave of Imam Husayn on the Day of Arafah if one cannot perform Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the concept of *Hajj al-Bada'il* (substitute pilgrimage), where visiting the shrine of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) serves as a valid substitute for the obligatory Hajj for those unable to travel to Mecca. The scholar Ibn Qulawayh uses this to emphasize the spiritual equivalence of the Imam's grave to the Kaaba, particularly when the pilgrim performs the *Tawaf* and stands in a state of reverence akin to the *Arafah* station. This ruling underscores the unique status of the Ahl al-Bayt in Shia jurisprudence as intermediaries of divine grace and spiritual fulfillment.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 8. Muḥammad ibn Ḥasan narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Ḥasan Al-Saffār, from Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā ibn ‘Ubayd, from Abī Sa’īd Al-Qammāť, from Ibn Abī Ya’fūr, who said:

I heard Abā ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) say: If one decides to go to Hajj but does not have the means to do so and goes to (the Ziyārah of) the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.) instead, and spends the Day of ‘Arafah next to his grave, his Ziyārah will suffice as having performed Hajj.
